arguments.value: Ford and iVillage made a 1998 sponsorship deal in which iVillage would build, host, and promote a Ford-branded site and related online marketing across the iVillage network, while Ford would pay setup and quarterly fees. iVillage had to create content, ads, polls, chats, sweepstakes, message boards, and other promotions, and provide regular traffic and performance reports. Ford got approval rights over the site and ads, exclusivity as the only auto manufacturer sponsor on the network during the term, and a license to use Ford marks; iVillage received rights to the materials it created for Ford, except for its own pre-existing software and tools. The agreement includes renewal options, performance/make-good or refund remedies if promised impressions are missed, confidentiality, mutual indemnities, limits on liability, termination rights for breach, insolvency, underperformance, or major Ford labor disruptions, and it is governed by New York law.
